result.summary: The pedestrian environment is significantly impacted by an overhead rail structure, which creates deep shadows and utilizes large support pillars that obstruct sightlines at the intersection. While basic infrastructure like marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals are present, the physical layout forces pedestrians to navigate around massive structural elements that hide them from oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Structural Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Large steel support pillars for the elevated rail structure are positioned near the crossing, blocking the view between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and right foreground, supporting the blue overhead structure

hazards.name: Low Ambient Light/Shadows
hazards.description: The overhead structure creates a dark environment and heavy shadows that reduce the visibility of pedestrians to motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway area directly under the blue steel structure

hazards.name: Degraded Road Surface
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven pavement within the crosswalk area increases trip hazards and may affect vehicle braking.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground roadway surface within the zebra markings

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway to move pedestrians past the pillars before they begin crossing, significantly improving mutual visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Underdeck Lighting
interventions.description: Install high-intensity LED lighting on the underside of the rail structure specifically aimed at the crosswalks to eliminate shadows.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines around the structural pillars.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is situated under an elevated transit structure, which provides shelter but creates significant visual obstructions due to large support pillars. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks, curb ramps, and pedestrian signals are present, the crosswalk markings are faded and the overall environment is shadowed and industrial.

hazards.name: Structural Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Large steel support pillars for the elevated structure block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians at the crossing point.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line and roadway edge

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk is significantly worn, reducing its visibility to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface at the intersection

hazards.name: Poor Lighting and Shadows
hazards.description: The elevated structure creates deep shadows and a dark environment that can obscure pedestrians even during daylight.
hazards.location_in_image: Underneath the elevated transit tracks

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install continental-style high-visibility crosswalk markings to improve driver awareness of the crossing zone.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to move pedestrians past the visual obstruction of the pillars before they enter the travel lane.

interventions.title: Enhanced Pedestrian Lighting
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale LED lighting under the structure to eliminate dark spots and improve personal security.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features marked zebra crosswalks, curb ramps with tactile warnings, and a median refuge under an elevated rail structure. However, the massive support columns create significant visual obstructions between drivers and pedestrians, and the overall crossing distance across multiple lanes remains substantial.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Infrastructure
hazards.description: Large steel support columns for the elevated rail block sightlines between turning vehicles and pedestrians in the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Center right, support columns near the crosswalk

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple travel lanes and a bike lane, increasing exposure to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground crosswalk

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility of pedestrians waiting to cross.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.

interventions.title: Enhanced Pedestrian Lighting
interventions.description: Add dedicated lighting under the elevated structure to illuminate the crosswalk area.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by an elevated rail structure that creates significant visual obstructions and a dark, shadowed environment. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and marked crosswalks are present, the massive pillars and wide roadway geometry increase risk for pedestrians by limiting sightlines.

hazards.name: Structural Pillar Obstructions
hazards.description: Large steel pillars for the elevated rail line significantly block sightlines between turning vehicles and pedestrians at the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the intersection area and along the curb line.

hazards.name: Low Light Environment
hazards.description: The elevated structure creates a dark, shadowed environment that reduces the visibility of pedestrians to drivers even during daylight hours.
hazards.location_in_image: Underneath the rail structure across the entire roadway.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalks to improve sightlines around the structural pillars for both drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Enhanced Pedestrian Lighting
interventions.description: Install additional high-intensity, pedestrian-scale lighting underneath the elevated structure to improve visibility in the shadowed areas.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade existing crosswalk markings to high-visibility 'continental' style using durable thermoplastic materials to improve driver awareness.
